---
title: "Teaching"
---
My teaching interests span foundational and advanced statistics. I connect statistical theory with real-world examples, helping students develop practical intuition alongside a rigorous theoretical foundation. My interests range from random variables, linear regression, analysis of variance, and experimental design to contemporary methods such as variational inference, Gaussian processes, and nonparametric spatial statistics. Alongside building a strong theoretical foundation, I emphasize reproducible, version-controlled programming and the ethical use of confidential and non-public data.

## Instructor of record
- **STAT 302: Statistical Methods**, Texas A&M University, Fall 2022.   
    I served as the instructor of record for an introductory statistics course with 43 students, covering probability distributions, point and interval estimation, and hypothesis testing. I also collaborated with instructors across STAT 302 sections to maintain consistent grading standards and develop common examinations.

## Teaching assistant

- **STAT 638: Applied Bayesian Methods**, Texas A&M University, Fall 2023.   
    As a teaching assistant, I helped convert multiple-choice examinations
    from an in-person format to Canvas, creating and carefully validating
    the online questions and answer choices. This transition streamlined
    assessment administration and established a reusable, consistent
    examination workflow.

- **STAT 641: Methods of Statistics I**, Texas A&M University, Spring 2020.   
    During the COVID-19 transition, I helped move homework submission and
    examination grading to eCampus. The centralized workflow simplified
    access to course materials, reduced reliance on email, and provided
    students with a consistent process for submitting assignments and
    receiving feedback.
